name: BMW M5 Competition
desc: The pinnacle of M engineering. The M5 Competition delivers raw power wrapped in pure luxury, with bespoke M-tuned suspension and ceramic brakes standard.

name: Audi RS7 Sportback
desc: Sculpted for the extraordinary. The RS7 Sportback merges fastback aesthetics with supercar performance — quattro AWD meets handcrafted interior opulence.

name: Mercedes-AMG GT 63 S
desc: Born on the Nürburgring. The AMG GT 63 S fuses brutal performance with 4-door practicality. Every surface tells a story of precision German engineering.

name: Porsche 911 GT3
desc: Purebred, naturally aspirated perfection. The 911 GT3 is Porsche's promise to motorsport lovers — a road-legal racing machine that sharpens every sense.

name: Ferrari Roma
desc: La Roma evokes the spirit of Italian elegance. A grand tourer born in Maranello, wrapping its 612hp heart in timeless coachwork that turns every street into a stage.

name: Lamborghini Urus S
desc: The Super SUV, elevated. Urus S delivers Lamborghini DNA in a form factor that conquers every terrain — from racetrack to mountain pass — without compromise.

name: Range Rover SV
desc: The ultimate expression of British luxury. Range Rover SV combines hand-stitched leather, rare wood veneers, and V8 authority in an icon that defines the class.

name: Tesla Model S Plaid
desc: The fastest production sedan on Earth. Model S Plaid rewrites physics with its Tri-Motor setup, delivering 1020hp and sub-2-second launches in utter silence.

name: Bentley Continental GT
desc: A symphony of handcraft and performance. The Continental GT is 100 hours of skilled craftsmanship, 659 horses, and enough presence to stop traffic on any continent.

name: Rolls-Royce Cullinan
desc: The first Rolls-Royce SUV. Named after the world's largest diamond, the Cullinan is the pinnacle of all-terrain luxury — truly effortless, everywhere.

name: McLaren 720S
desc: Carbon fiber wrapped fury. The 720S is McLaren's masterpiece — a mid-engine supercar with active aerodynamics and a twin-turbo V8 that rewrites road-car benchmarks.

name: Aston Martin Vantage
desc: 007's weapon of choice. The Vantage channels 90 years of British sports car heritage into a precision instrument — every curve is a design statement.

name: Porsche Cayenne Turbo GT
desc: The fastest SUV on the Nürburgring. Cayenne Turbo GT blends Porsche DNA with SUV practicality — nothing corners faster with seats for five.

name: BMW X7 M60i
desc: Seven-seat M performance redefined. The X7 M60i commands respect with its imposing kidney grille and M-tuned V8, wrapping occupants in bespoke Merino leather.

name: Mercedes S 680 Maybach
desc: The last word in automotive luxury. S 680 Maybach features rear-seat massage, Burmester 4D audio, and a hand-polished V12 draped in the finest Nappa leather.

name: Audi e-tron GT RS
desc: The electric grand tourer. RS e-tron GT blends quattro AWD with instant electric torque — 637hp launched silently, wrapped in Audi's sharpest design language yet.

name: Maserati MC20
desc: Renaissance of Italian performance. The MC20 carries the Nettuno engine — Maserati's first in-house engine since the GranTurismo MC12 — in a carbon fiber masterpiece.

name: Bugatti Chiron Sport
desc: Hyper art. The Chiron Sport is Bugatti's relentless pursuit of the absolute — 1500hp, 420km/h, and an interior that took 300+ hours to hand-craft in Molsheim.

name: Bentley Bentayga EWB
desc: Extended opulence. The EWB variant adds 180mm of rear legroom to Bentley's flagship SUV — First Class aviation seating in the world's most refined off-roader.

name: Lexus LC 500h
desc: Japanese luxury art form. The LC 500h sculpts the road with its silhouette before it even moves — a driver's grand tourer with origami-inspired bodywork.

name: BMW iX M60
desc: M Performance meets zero emission. The iX M60 proves electrification and driving excitement aren't opposites — 610hp in a SAV draped in sustainable luxury.

name: Mercedes EQS 580
desc: The electric S-Class. EQS 580 features the Hyperscreen — a 141cm curved OLED dashboard — paired with MBUX AI and 516hp of whisper-quiet German performance.

name: Porsche Taycan Turbo S
desc: Electrically, unmistakably Porsche. The Taycan Turbo S corners like the 911, launches like a catapult, and never asks you to compromise what a Porsche is supposed to feel like.

name: Rolls-Royce Ghost Black Badge
desc: A statement of confident non-conformity. Ghost Black Badge is for those who prefer to be noticed for what they are rather than what they have — still unmistakably Rolls-Royce.

name: Ferrari SF90 Stradale
desc: The most powerful road Ferrari ever built. SF90 Stradale's hybrid powertrain produces 986hp — a quantum leap that still carries Ferrari's soul in every rev.

name: Audi RS Q8
desc: The RS flagship SUV. With 591hp, adaptive air suspension, and quattro Sport Differential, the RS Q8 corners as sharply as it commands highway lanes.

name: Mercedes AMG C 63 S E
desc: The game-changer C-Class. AMG's new hybrid formula produces 671hp from a 4-cylinder — revolutionary technology in a compact, razor-sharp performance sedan.

name: BMW M8 Gran Coupe
desc: The ultimate 4-door coupe. M8 Gran Coupé delivers M8 Competition performance in a bespoke four-door silhouette — Merino leather and V8 thunder in perfect union.

name: Aston Martin DBX 707
desc: 707hp from Aston Martin's only SUV. The DBX 707 carries Bond's pedigree into the segment — no other luxury SUV accelerates, handles, or looks like this.

name: Maserati Levante GT
desc: Italian flair, global capability. The Levante GT brings Ferrari-derived engine architecture and tri-zone climate control to an SUV that refuses to be ordinary.

name: Lamborghini Huracán EVO
desc: Naturally aspirated fury. The Huracán EVO's 5.2L V10 screams to 8700rpm — a sound and sensation no turbo or electric powertrain can replicate.

name: Lexus LX 600 F Sport
desc: Japanese precision meets Land Cruiser toughness. LX 600 F Sport wraps the legendary LC200 platform in Lexus's sharpest design, with off-road capability to match its interior grandeur.

name: Cadillac Escalade V
desc: American luxury, supercharged. Escalade-V packs 682hp under its massive hood while offering 19-speaker AKG audio and a 38-inch curved OLED cockpit inside.

name: Porsche Panamera Turbo S
desc: Four-seat sports car. The Panamera Turbo S defies physics — 620hp, rear-axle steering, and Porsche Active Suspension in a luxury executive saloon.

name: Ferrari Purosangue
desc: Ferrari dared to build an SUV — and produced a masterpiece. The Purosangue is the only naturally-aspirated V12 SUV ever made, wearing Ferrari's Fiorano DNA throughout.

name: Bugatti W16 Mistral
desc: The final W16. Mistral is Bugatti's farewell to the legendary W16 engine — 1600hp in a roadster form, with only 99 examples destined for the most discerning collectors.

name: Genesis GV80 Coupe
desc: Korea's luxury gambit. Genesis GV80 Coupé brings quilted Nappa leather, Lexicon audio, and European-rivalling dynamics at a price that makes competitors uncomfortable.

name: Lincoln Navigator Black Label
desc: American presidential transport. Lincoln Navigator Black Label offers a 'Destination: Haven' interior theme with Perfect Position captain's chairs and an 800W Revel audio system.

name: Bentley Flying Spur
desc: The world's most desirable saloon. Flying Spur's cabin features 109 cross-stitched diamonds per leather panel — 400,000 stitches crafted entirely by hand.

name: McLaren Artura
desc: McLaren's hybrid future arrives. The Artura is built on an all-new carbon architecture — lighter than the 720S, and with plug-in hybrid tech, cleaner than anything McLaren has built.

name: BMW 7 Series M760e
desc: The new 7 Series is BMW's boldest flagship yet — Theatre Screen in the rear, executive lounge seating, and a hybrid V8 that defies its limousine proportions.

name: Infiniti QX80 Premium
desc: Japanese luxury, American proportion. QX80 Premium's reimagined cabin delivers semi-aniline leather, open-pore wood, and a 23-speaker Klipsch audio system.

name: Mercedes GLS 600 Maybach
desc: The Maybach experience, elevated to an SUV. GLS 600 Maybach transforms every road into first-class travel — fridge, massage seats, and Burmester Surround included.

name: Aston Martin DB12
desc: 'The World's First Super Tourer.' DB12 is Aston's complete reinvention — double the performance of DB11, with a new chassis, new interior, and 671hp from an AMG-sourced V8.

name: Lamborghini Revuelto
desc: The Aventador successor arrives. Revuelto pairs Lamborghini's iconic V12 with three electric motors for 1015hp — the most powerful Lamborghini ever built, and the most beautiful.

name: Porsche 718 Cayman GT4 RS
desc: Mid-engine motorsport derived. The 718 Cayman GT4 RS borrows its flat-6 directly from the 911 GT3 — installed sideways in the most precise sports car Porsche makes.

name: Alfa Romeo Giulia GTA
desc: 100 examples. The Giulia GTA uses carbon fiber doors, hood and roof to save 100kg vs standard — paired with a 540hp Ferrari-developed V6 and racing-inspired aero.

name: BMW M4 CSL
desc: Coupe Sport Leichtbau. The M4 CSL sheds 100kg versus M4 Competition via carbon fiber panels and deleted rear seats — the most hardcore road-going M4 ever sanctioned.

name: Jaguar F-Type R75
desc: 75 years of British sports car heritage. The F-Type R75 is Jaguar's farewell edition — 575hp of supercharged V8 soundtrack, wearing Arden Green and 20-inch gloss black wheels.

name: Mercedes SL 63 AMG
desc: The legend reborn. SL 63 AMG returns as a 2+2 roadster developed entirely by AMG — softtop, V8, rear-axle steering, and an MBUX Hyperscreen cockpit worthy of its heritage.

name: Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing
desc: America's last great performance sedan. CT5-V Blackwing's 668hp supercharged V8 out-muscles BMW M5, costs $90k less, and comes standard with Brembo carbon ceramics.

name: Alfa Romeo Stelvio Quadrifoglio
desc: The SUV for those who think SUVs are boring. Stelvio Quadrifoglio's Ferrari-derived V6 and carbon fiber driveshaft set the Nürburgring SUV lap record — by 10 seconds.

name: Maserati Grecale Trofeo
desc: MC20's engine in an SUV. The Grecale Trofeo transplants Maserati's race-derived Nettuno V6 into a daily-usable SUV — 523hp that transforms school runs into occasions.

name: BMW M3 Competition xDrive
desc: The eternal benchmark. M3 Competition xDrive combines the S58's 503hp with BMW's xDrive AWD — all-weather M performance in the world's most iconic sports sedan.

name: Audi RS5 Sportback
desc: The practical performance four-door. RS5 Sportback serves 444hp through quattro AWD with five seats and a hatchback boot — the thinking person's sports car choice.

name: Mercedes E 53 AMG
desc: AMG's sweet spot. E 53 pairs a mild-hybrid 6-cylinder with AMG suspension tuning — the perfect balance of daily luxury and spirited performance in the new-generation E-Class body.

name: Porsche Macan EV
desc: The electric Macan arrives, and it's properly Porsche. Built on the PPE platform shared with Audi, Macan EV delivers 630hp and 600km range without losing its sports car soul.

name: Range Rover Sport P530
desc: The Sport name earns its place. Range Rover Sport P530 is the driver's Range Rover — 530hp V8, adaptive air suspension, and a class-leading tow capacity for those who do everything.

name: Genesis G90 Luxury
desc: Korea's answer to the S-Class. Genesis G90 offers massage seats, 21-speaker Bang & Olufsen audio, and a Luxury Package that embarrasses cars costing twice as much.

name: Ferrari 296 GTB
desc: The future of Ferrari. 296 GTB introduces a new 6-cylinder era for Ferrari with 819hp hybrid performance — and proves the V6 can be a spiritual successor to the V8.

name: Lamborghini Sterrato
desc: An off-road Lamborghini. The Sterrato raises the Huracán body, adds rally-spec tires and underbody protection — creating the world's only 602hp off-road supercar.

name: Porsche 918 Spyder
desc: Holy Trinity member. The 918 Spyder is one of only 918 examples of Porsche's hypercar masterstroke — 887hp hybrid technology that set a production car Nürburgring record.

name: McLaren 765LT
desc: Longtail, lighter, faster. The 765LT is 80kg lighter than the 720S with 755hp and a titanium exhaust — only 765 built, all sold before announcement.

name: Aston Martin Valkyrie
desc: F1 for the road. Valkyrie was designed by Adrian Newey — the same aerodynamicist who creates Red Bull F1 cars. Its naturally-aspirated V12 revs to 11,100rpm.

name: BMW M2
desc: The purist's choice. M2 brings M4's S58 engine to the smallest M car — optional 6-speed manual, rear-wheel drive, and a price that makes driving excitement accessible.

name: Audi TT RS Final Edition
desc: The final chapter. TT RS Final Edition bids farewell to Audi's most iconic sports coupe with carbon styling package, exclusive color, and the best 5-cylinder ever built.

name: Mercedes CLE 53 AMG
desc: E-Class meets AMG in coupe form. The CLE 53 is the new pillarless coupe in Mercedes lineup — sophisticated mild-hybrid performance in a genuinely beautiful two-door body.

name: Porsche 992 Carrera GTS
desc: GTS now with hybrid power. The 992 Carrera GTS becomes the first 911 with T-Hybrid technology — 532hp from 3.0L and an electric exhaust turbine for zero-lag response.

name: Ferrari 812 Superfast
desc: The last naturally-aspirated V12 Ferrari GT. 812 Superfast produces 789hp at 8500rpm — a sound and fury that marks the end of an era in the most dramatic fashion possible.

name: Porsche 959
desc: The car that invented the supercar. Porsche 959 from 1987 remains one of the greatest automotive engineering achievements — AWD, twin-turbo, and ABS when none of these existed.

name: Bentley Mulliner Batur
desc: 18 examples only. Mulliner Batur is Bentley's vision of a future GT — 730hp W12, completely bespoke commission, and the final hurrah for the iconic Continental's W12 chapter.

name: Lamborghini Sián FKP 37
desc: Lamborghini's first hybrid hypercar. Only 63 Sián examples built — each bespoke — featuring V12 power augmented by a supercapacitor 34hp motor. The rarest Sant'Agata creation.

name: Rolls-Royce Spectre
desc: The first all-electric Rolls-Royce. Spectre is the most aerodynamic Rolls-Royce ever built — 577hp in utter silence, featuring over 1700 star lights in the headliner.

name: Ferrari Daytona SP3
desc: Icona series masterpiece. Ferrari Daytona SP3 is a rolling tribute to the 312P's 1967 Daytona 24H win — open-top, 829hp V12, and only 599 examples destined for collectors.

name: McLaren Solus GT
desc: Track only, one of 25. Solus GT emerged from the Gran Turismo video game as a real car — a single-seat pure racing car with 829hp V10 for private track days.

name: Audi RS3 Sedan
desc: 400hp compact sedan. RS3's five-cylinder turbo is one of motoring's great sounds — 394hp in a car that's smaller than a Golf but faster than a V8 muscle car.

name: Mercedes A 45 S AMG
desc: The world's most powerful 2.0L production engine. A 45 S squeezes 421hp from two liters — delivering AMG's most attainable supercar experience in a practical hatchback.

name: BMW M135i xDrive
desc: M Performance at its most accessible. M135i brings xDrive and 306hp to a family-friendly hatchback — the daily driver that never lets you forget it's a BMW M car.

name: Audi S5 Sportback
desc: quattro SQ5. The S5 Sportback blends corporate sophistication with sports performance — 349hp V6, quattro drive, and a five-door fastback body that flatters any setting.

name: Mercedes C 43 AMG
desc: AMG's modern compact. C 43 AMG uses mild hybrid technology and 402hp from a 4-cylinder to deliver genuine AMG dynamics in the newest C-Class body — with all the tech.

name: Jaguar F-PACE SVR
desc: V8 supercharged SUV from Coventry. F-PACE SVR delivers supercharged drama with a 543hp V8 soundtrack that only Jaguar builds — wrapped in distinctive SVR aero and Alcantara.

name: Maserati Quattroporte Trofeo
desc: The Italian grand saloon. Quattroporte Trofeo's Ferrari-developed V8 produces 580hp in one of the most emotionally resonant four-door saloons in the world.

name: Ferrari Portofino M
desc: The Ferrari for everyday. Portofino M is the most approachable Ferrari — a retractable hardtop convertible delivering 612hp in a grand touring package that doubles as daily transport.

name: Rolls-Royce Dawn
desc: The most social Rolls-Royce. Dawn's soft top lowers in 22 seconds to reveal a sumptuous 4-seat open-air experience — designed for those who want to see and be seen.

name: Aston Martin Valhalla
desc: Between Vantage and Valkyrie. Valhalla is Aston's hybrid hypercar — 937hp, F1-derived active aero, and a carbon fiber monocoque designed with Red Bull Advanced Technologies.

name: BMW i7 M70 xDrive
desc: M Performance in the electric 7 Series. i7 M70 delivers 650hp and a 31-inch rear Theatre Screen — executive luxury at the forefront of BMW's electric future.

name: Porsche Cayenne E-Hybrid
desc: Electrified Cayenne performance. The new E-Hybrid dramatically increases electric range while maintaining Cayenne's signature sports SUV dynamics — the future of Porsche SUVs.

name: Mercedes EQS SUV 680
desc: The AMG version of Mercedes' electric flagship SUV. EQS 680 SUV seats 7 in near-silence with 649hp and a Hyperscreen dashboard that spans the entire dashboard width.

name: Lamborghini Urus Performante
desc: The apex super SUV. Urus Performante drops 47kg versus standard through carbon fiber aero kit, titanium exhaust, and Pirelli P Zero Corsa tires — the Nürburgring SUV record holder.

name: Ferrari GTC4Lusso
desc: The four-seat Ferrari. GTC4Lusso carries four in a shooting brake body with four-wheel drive and 680hp V12 — perhaps the most practical Ferrari ever conceived.

name: Koenigsegg Agera RS
desc: The car that shattered records. Agera RS set the outright production car speed record at 277mph in Nevada. Only 25 built — every one a unique customer specification.

name: Pagani Huayra Roadster BC
desc: Rolling art by Pagani. Huayra Roadster BC is crafted from Carbotitanio — carbon and titanium composite — with a hand-assembled AMG V12 in a body that weighs just 1218kg.

name: Bugatti Veyron 16.4 Super Sport
desc: The fastest production car of its era. Veyron Super Sport set 267mph in 2010 and held the record for three years. A collector piece that defined an automotive generation.

name: Mercedes SLS AMG Electric Drive
desc: Ultra-rare gull-wing EV. SLS AMG Electric Drive was Mercedes' first all-electric supercar — 740hp from four motors in a carbon fiber chassis, with gull-wing doors. Only 19 built.

name: BMW M5 CS
desc: The pinnacle M5. CS (Club Sport) sheds 70kg versus Competition via carbon fiber roof, hood, and bucket seats — 627hp in BMW's most track-focused four-door ever.

name: Lamborghini Aventador SVJ
desc: The ALA SVJ. Aventador SVJ's Aerodinamica Lamborghini Attiva system actively adjusts aerodynamics in 500ms — 770hp in a car that set the production car Nürburgring record.

name: Ferrari LaFerrari
desc: The rarest Ferrari of modern times. LaFerrari used F1 KERS technology in a road car — 950hp in one of only 499 coupes, each personally assigned by Enzo Ferrari's successors.

name: McLaren P1
desc: Holy Trinity's F1 successor. McLaren P1 completed the Holy Trinity alongside LaFerrari and 918 Spyder — 903hp hybrid hypercar engineered to be the fastest production car around any circuit.

name: Porsche Taycan Cross Turismo
desc: The electric sport turismo. Taycan Cross Turismo adds a raised wagon body to Porsche's electric sports car — all the excitement, plus 81L more luggage space and light off-road capability.

name: Bentley Speed 6 Concept
desc: Bentley reimagines Speed 6. Drawing from the legendary 1920s Speed Six that won Le Mans, this modern interpretation channels Bentley's racing heritage in 750hp of W12 grand touring.

name: Audi R8 V10 Performance
desc: The last R8 ever. Audi R8 V10 Performance is one of the final Neckarsulm-built R8s — a mid-engine naturally-aspirated V10 masterpiece that ends Audi's supercar chapter.

name: Bugatti Tourbillon
desc: Chiron's successor. The Bugatti Tourbillon arrives with a 1800hp naturally-aspirated V16 hybrid — the most complex engine ever installed in a production car, inspired by Cosworth F1 technology.
